question: Why does Code Search have to return every match for broad queries when web search can just show top-ranked items, and how does the codebase sharding help keep typical searches fast?
reference_answer: Code Search must deliver all results for tooling and developer trust, unlike web search, which can take shortcuts by considering only highly ranked items. Since adding characters to a Code Search query always narrows the result set, short queries can match enormous numbers of files, so the system splits the codebase into priority-ordered shards and usually only considers high-priority matches, fetching complete results only when requested.
